To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fungus Colletotrichium acutatum causes citrus postbloom fruit-drop (PBFD) by triggering the expression of ethylene and jasmonic acid (JA) biosynthetic genes, as well as genes for indole-3 acetic acid (IA) regulation, in citrus flower petals.

infection of citrus flowers by the fungus Colletotrichurn acutatum triggers differential expression of genes encoding proteins related to hormone biosynthesis and regulation, as well as increases the concentrations of hormones in the flowers.

infection of citrus flowers by the fungus Colletotrichun acutatum triggers the differential expression of genes associated with phytohormone production and regulation, as well as increased hormone levels, consistent with a hypothesis of the involvement phytohormons in postbloom drop.

the identification of genes involved in the regulation of phytohorns and their role in citrus postbloom fruit-drop.
the identification of genes involved in the biosynthesis, regulation and signal transduction of phytohromones, and their role in symptom development of postbloom fruit disease in citrus.
the molecular biology of citrus fruit drop, which is the most economically important disease of citrus.
